slides.eyebrow: SOURCE CONCEPT · REASON THROUGH THE MECHANISM
keyPoints: APPENDIX · PRIMARY SOURCES FOR GRADUATE EXTENSIONS
slides.narration:
The ABI example is deliberately restricted to ordinary two-int argument passing and an int result. The System V AMD64 reference and Microsoft's x64 documentation support that comparison; neither table in this lecture claims to be a complete ABI specification. Linux manual pages support the Linux-specific image replacement, dynamic loading, mapping, output, and termination discussion. The ELF program-header reference supplies the segment-versus-section distinction used in the loading extension.

The sanitizer references document the scope and use of two complementary diagnostic tools. They do not turn a clean test run into a proof of whole-program correctness. These platform-specific sources are identified as such so that readers do not mistake the Linux/GNU examples for universal C language requirements. The lecture package also records the actual compiler environment used for its companion build test. All reference codes resolve to full primary-source entries in the notes and References.md.

In plain English: Different handoffs have different rulebooks. Check the one that matches the function call, operating-system request, or testing tool.

The ABI example is deliberately restricted to ordinary two-int argument passing and an int result. slides.title: API, ABI, and ISA locate three kinds of agreement
slides.eyebrow: 01 / SYSTEMS REASONING
slides.narration: Suppose two components agree that add takes two integers and returns an integer. That source-facing promise is part of the API. They must also agree about where compiled arguments and results are placed. That is an ABI question. The machine instructions used to perform the addition belong to the ISA. The same x86-64 instruction set can support different calling conventions, so sharing an ISA does not automatically make arbitrary compiled components compatible. A header helps align source declarations, but it does not by itself repair a wrong binary calling convention. When diagnosing a boundary, name the kind of agreement and inspect evidence at that level.
actions: Give students a function signature and ask what it does not specify about compiled calls.
slides.sourceRef: content/systems-programming/ch1.json → SP01.010 / API, ABI, and ISA answer different questions

question.prompt: Can two components target x86-64 and still disagree about argument passing?
question.answer: Yes. Different ABIs can use different calling conventions on the same ISA.

slides.title: Relocation is unfinished address arithmetic
slides.eyebrow: 01 / SYSTEMS REASONING
keyPoints: An object file can contain unresolved references
The linker combines symbols and placement
Loader work is a later boundary
slides.narration: A separately compiled caller may contain a request to call a function whose final location is not yet known. The object file records enough information for later work, including symbols and relocations. A relocation tells a tool how to finish an address-dependent calculation after placement or binding information is available. It is not evidence that the function body is already in the caller's source file. The linker combines compiled responsibilities, while loading later establishes a process image. A successfully linked file still needs a compatible execution environment and runtime resources. This chain explains why inspecting only the source or only the final output can miss the boundary where a defect begins.
actions: Ask learners to identify what an object file may defer to later stages.
slides.sourceRef: content/systems-programming/ch1.json → SP01.024 / Relocation: finish an address-dependent calculation

question.prompt: Why can an object file exist even when the final function address is not known?
question.answer: It can record symbolic references and relocation information for later resolution.

slides.title: Optimization preserves required behavior, not source appearance
slides.eyebrow: 01 / SYSTEMS REASONING
keyPoints: A variable need not keep a permanent RAM slot
An operation may be folded or removed
Invalid source behavior breaks the reasoning contract
slides.narration: The expression x plus three describes a source-level computation. If x is a known constant, the compiler may replace the calculation with its result. If a local value need not be stored, it may remain in a register or disappear into another instruction. This does not mean the compiler ignored the program; it means source appearance is not the required physical schedule. To judge a transformation, begin with defined source behavior and observable requirements. An out-of-bounds read is not made valid by an optimization setting that happens to print the expected value. When comparing assembly, connect changes to behavior and assumptions rather than counting source statements as if each required one instruction.
actions: Trace one constant expression and one input-dependent expression into possible implementations.
slides.sourceRef: content/systems-programming/ch1.json → SP01.021 / Optimization does not preserve source appearance

question.prompt: Does removing a source variable from assembly prove a compiler defect?
question.answer: No. The compiler may eliminate or combine representations while preserving required observable behavior for defined executions.

slides.title: A local speedup has a whole-program limit
slides.eyebrow: 01 / SYSTEMS REASONING
keyPoints: Keep unchanged work in the calculation
Report a derived bound separately from a measurement
slides.narration: Suppose forty percent of elapsed work can become four times faster and sixty percent is unchanged. Normalize the original time to one. The new model time is sixty hundredths plus forty hundredths divided by four, which is seventy hundredths. The modeled overall speedup is one divided by seventy hundredths, about one point four three. It is not four times. This calculation assumes the fractions and costs remain comparable and ignores new overhead. It is a derived estimate, not a timing measurement of this lecture program. Real measurements need a workload, build settings, machine conditions, and repeated observations. The model helps us decide whether an optimization is worth investigating.
actions: Compute the normalized new time before naming the speedup.
slides.sourceRef: content/systems-programming/ch1.json → SP01.040 / Derive the limit of a local speedup

question.prompt: What portion remains even if the improved 40 percent becomes infinitely fast?
question.answer: The unchanged 60 percent remains, limiting speedup to about 1.67 under this model.

slides.title: Partial success changes what a correct retry means
slides.eyebrow: 01 / SYSTEMS REASONING
keyPoints: A result may report progress and remaining work
Keep ownership valid while handling failure
slides.narration: Imagine an interface asked to process ten bytes but reporting that four were accepted. A retry of the original ten can duplicate the first four. The next request must describe the remaining six, beginning at the correct position, if that is the interface's documented progress model. This is a robustness problem because the state after partial success matters as much as the happy path. It is also an ownership problem: the buffer must remain alive while the remainder is used. A boolean success flag would lose important information here. The chapter's broader lesson is to define failure and partial-progress states explicitly, then make recovery follow those states.
actions: Have learners draw the completed prefix and remaining suffix of ten bytes.
slides.sourceRef: content/systems-programming/ch1.json → SP01.047 / Partial success changes the retry position

question.prompt: Why is a simple success/failure boolean sometimes too weak for I/O?
question.answer: It can hide how much work completed, so the caller cannot safely choose a retry position or distinguish no progress from partial progress.

slides.title: Defend the boundary, assumptions, and evidence
slides.eyebrow: 01 / SYSTEMS REASONING
keyPoints: Choose an artifact that can test the hypothesis
Do not expand one observation into a universal claim
slides.narration: For a final check, explain a program that compiles, links, starts, and then rejects an input file. The earlier successes establish different facts: language checking passed, required compiled pieces were connected, and the executable began running in this environment. They do not establish permission to read this particular file or that its contents obey a format. Now name the next evidence you would gather without printing unrelated secrets. A path, error status, and expected access contract can be useful. This style of explanation scales from a twelve-line example to a large service because it narrows the responsible boundary before proposing a repair.
actions: Ask each learner for one claim, one assumption, and one matching piece of evidence.

question.prompt: What should a strong diagnosis include beyond the sentence it did not work?
question.answer: The first failed boundary, its expected contract, the relevant assumptions, and evidence that supports or rejects a specific explanation.

example.title: One request crosses several layers
explain: const makes total read-only after initialization. int is the whole-number type. The + expression adds 7 and 5 at execution; = initializes the named result to 12. The compiler checks the types and may precompute this constant expression.
std:: names the standard-library namespace. ostringstream is an output stream that collects formatted text in an owned string rather than writing it immediately to a terminal.
For streams, << inserts the value on its right into the stream on its left. The quoted label is text; total supplies the number to format.
message.str() returns the collected text. std::cout sends it to standard output, and the character literal \n supplies a newline. The operating system handles the underlying output service.
assert checks a Boolean condition during this verification build and stops the program if it is false. It does not prove the program correct for inputs the test never tried.
example.invariant: The arithmetic result is independent of its text label. Both inputs and their sum fit in int.
